To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have presented a novel approach for morphological inflections, which we show to be state of the art, and that we provide an analysis of attention models.

1) hard attention is a viable alternative to soft attention for morphological inflections, 2) the hard attention model is more interpretable than its soft counterpart, 3) the hard attention is a good choice for morphological inflectors, and 4) the hard attention inflector is a good choice to generate inflections for words that do not appear in the training data.

1) a hard monotonic attention model is able to outperform state of the art approaches on morphological inflection datasets, 2) the attention mechanism learns to focus on the correct part of the input, 3) the model learns to focus on a small number of characters in the inflection and to ignore the rest, 4) the model learns a representation of the input that is able to predict the output, and 5) the model learns the same representation for the input
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we leverage the monotonicity of morphological inflection to build a neural inflection model which is simpler and more effective than previous approaches?
two main topics: the use of hard attention in neural sequence-to-sequence models and the study of the features learned by attention mechanisms.
two questions: (i) Can we learn morphological inflection from data using a simple attention mechanism? and (ii) What can we learn about attention models from the morphological inflection task?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hard attention models are better for inflection generation, but soft attention is more flexible.
the hard attention model performs better than the soft attention model in the task of morphological inflection.
hard monotonic attention is a viable alternative to soft attention in morphological inflection tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hard monotonic attention mechanism is able to capture and learn the nearly-monotone alignment between the characters in the word and the characters of its inflection.
the hard monotonic attention model is a very strong baseline for morphological inflections generation.
we propose a novel neural network for the task which achieves state of the art performance and we show that the attention mechanism is able to learn meaningful alignments for the task.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the hard attention mechanism, while being less flexible than the soft one, is able to achieve state-of-the-art results on morphological inflection tasks, and is able to learn representations that are similar to those of the soft attention model.
the use of hard attention is beneficial for morphological inflections, as it allows to better capture the nearly-monotonical alignment.
hard attention can be a viable alternative to soft attention in tasks involving alignment between sequences.
